title: IB Biology Revision Plan: Three Weeks to November
summary: IB Biology revision plan for the final three weeks before November exams, with topic triage, timed practice, error review, recovery, and smart rest.
body_markdown:
Three weeks can feel uncomfortably short. Yet it is enough time to make a meaningful difference, provided you stop treating every Biology topic as equally urgent.


This **IB Biology revision plan** works backwards from your first November Biology exam. Week one diagnoses and repairs weaknesses. Week two converts knowledge into marks through mixed questions. Week three rehearses the exam while protecting sleep and attention. If you are taking several subjects, Biology should occupy focused blocks rather than consume every available hour.


The aim is not to relearn the entire syllabus. It is to make your remaining study time increasingly similar to what the exam requires.


### Your three-week plan at a glance


Period Main priority Recommended Biology workload


Week one Diagnose gaps and repair high-priority topics 60-90 minutes on five days


Week two Mixed questions, data analysis and answer quality 75-105 minutes on five days


Week three Timed papers, correction and recovery 45-90 minutes, adjusted around exams


Use this checklist before beginning:


- Find the exact dates of your Biology papers and other November exams.
- List every syllabus topic and label it green, amber or red.
- Complete a short mixed diagnostic set without notes.
- Create one error log for the entire three weeks.
- Reserve at least one lighter evening each week.
- Schedule two full timed Biology sessions before the exam.


The[IB Biology November exam dates and planning guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-biology-november-2026-exam-dates) can help you place these tasks around your actual timetable. Count backwards from your own first Biology paper rather than assuming that Monday must be day one.


### Week one: Find where the marks are hiding


The first week is about triage. A red topic is not simply one you dislike. It is a topic where weak understanding is likely to cost marks and where focused revision can still produce improvement.


Begin with 25-40 mixed questions under light time pressure. Include rapid-response questions, data interpretation and written explanations. The current IB Biology assessment includes Paper 1A, Paper 1B and Paper 2, so your diagnosis should test more than factual recall. This[comparison of IB Biology Paper 1 and Paper 2](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-biology-paper-1-vs-paper-2) explains the different demands.


Sort each mistake into one of four categories:


Error type What it means Best response


Knowledge gap You did not know the relevant biology Review concise Study Notes, then retrieve it from memory


Application gap You knew the idea but could not use it Answer several unfamiliar questions on the same concept


Data gap You misread a graph, table or experimental setup Practise identifying variables, trends and valid conclusions


Communication gap Your response was vague or incomplete Compare command terms and rewrite the answer precisely


Now rank your red topics. Prioritize ideas that connect to several parts of the course, frequently appear in mixed questions or repeatedly break down in your answers. Use RevisionDojo **Study Notes** for concise repair, **Flashcards** for retrieval and **AI Chat** when one step in a process remains unclear. Then move quickly into the[IB Biology Questionbank for Form and Function](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-biology-new/ib-biology-new-b-form-and-function/questionbank) or another relevant theme.


A practical weekday block might contain 20 minutes of recall, 30 minutes of questions and 15 minutes of correction. Finish by writing three things you can now explain without help. Your error log, not the number of hours studied, is the real record of progress.


### Week two: Turn understanding into usable answers


By week two, reading should become secondary. Biology examinations reward knowledge that survives contact with unfamiliar wording, new data and time pressure.


Use alternating sessions:


- **Session A:** mixed Paper 1A-style questions followed by immediate correction.
- **Session B:** data-based Paper 1B-style work, including graph interpretation and experimental reasoning.
- **Session C:** structured and extended Paper 2-style responses.
- **Session D:** targeted repair of the two weakest areas revealed by Sessions A-C.
- **Session E:** one longer mixed set completed under timed conditions.


RevisionDojo's[Test Builder and Exam Mode](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/test-builder) are useful here. Build targeted sets early in the week, then remove topic filters and use Exam mode later. Complete every answer before revealing guidance. The habit of checking after each uncertain line feels productive, but it prevents you from discovering whether you can sustain an explanation independently.


Use the **grading tools** to identify missing biological detail, then rewrite weak responses from a blank page. If you want to understand what distinguishes secure knowledge from consistently precise answers, read[the difference between a 6 and 7 in IB Biology](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/difference-between-6-and-7-ib-biology) .


You can also use **Predicted Papers** and **Mock Exams** to experience unfamiliar combinations of questions. Treat scores as diagnostic signals, not prophecies. A low score that reveals three repairable patterns is more valuable than a comfortable set containing only familiar material.


A student points to a November calendar while a tiny lung-costumed figure celebrates a deliberately empty revision slot.


### Week three: Rehearse, correct and taper


The final week should become narrower, not louder. This is where students often respond to anxiety by expanding their workload precisely when judgment and sleep matter most.


Complete two timed sessions using the format and conditions you will face. At least one should combine material from across the course. Use Exam mode, clear your desk, silence your phone and follow the permitted-material rules communicated by your school and the IB. The[November Biology mock preparation guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-biology-mock-exam-prep-november) offers a broader framework for realistic rehearsal.


Correction deserves its own session. For every lost mark, record the topic, error type and corrected reasoning. Then choose only three repair priorities. Trying to fix twenty small weaknesses at once usually produces shallow review of all twenty.


A sensible final-week rhythm is:


- **Seven to five days before:** sit the first timed set and correct it fully.
- **Four to three days before:** repair recurring errors with short Questionbank sets.
- **Two days before:** complete a final timed section, not necessarily another full paper.
- **One day before:** review the error log, practise brief retrieval and prepare materials.
- **Exam morning:** use a short confidence review, then stop.


The[realistic final week before exams](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/realistic-final-week-before-exams) is a useful companion if several subjects collide. Do not sacrifice sleep to complete one more set. Tired revision can create the feeling of effort while weakening recall, reading accuracy and decision-making the next day.


### Keep the plan flexible across several subjects


Imagine that Biology is on Thursday, but Mathematics is on Tuesday and a language paper follows on Friday. A rigid daily Biology schedule would ignore the real constraint: your attention belongs to several subjects.


Use three block sizes instead:


- **Full block, 75-90 minutes:** timed work or a difficult topic repair.
- **Standard block, 45-60 minutes:** mixed questions plus correction.
- **Maintenance block, 20-30 minutes:** Flashcards, diagrams and error-log retrieval.


On a heavy day for another subject, choose maintenance. After an exam, take a genuine break before deciding whether a standard block is realistic. If coursework questions are still distracting you, RevisionDojo's **Coursework Library** can clarify expectations, while **Tutors** provide focused support when a misconception resists independent study. These tools should remove bottlenecks rather than enlarge your schedule.


Rest also belongs inside the plan. Keep one lighter evening each week, take short movement breaks and establish a stopping time. A timetable without recovery is not ambitious. It is incomplete.


### Enter November with evidence, not guesswork


Confidence rarely arrives because every page has been reread. It grows when you can point to evidence: weak topics identified, questions attempted, errors corrected and timed work completed.


For the next three weeks, keep the loop simple: diagnose, repair, practise, review and rest. Use RevisionDojo as the central IB resource connecting **Study Notes, Flashcards, AI Chat, grading tools, Predicted Papers, Mock Exams, the Coursework Library and Tutors** . Most importantly, practise deliberately in the **Questionbank** and sit timed papers in **Exam mode** .


The calendar may be short. Your decisions can still be precise.
